problems.location: l.83, 'Below the discovery size the same plot is flat: for h6_10 at n=128 ... the sign agrees on 0.70 of the points, the majority rate.'

problems.location: l.285 (Blank pixels), l.295 (Reading: 'digits are told apart largely by where they are open'), l.313 (Summary: 'Much of the evidence in its maps lies on blank pixels')

problems.location: l.297, 'the most gain goes to contrasts of very different silhouettes ... Similar-looking classes get almost none'
problems.problem: The examples come only from Fashion and MNIST. On qd_dev the top class pair by gain per drawn pair is grapes–soccer ball (5.31×, 3 drawn), two round shapes that are qd_dev's third most confused pair (verify-reading:image C9). The negative relation with confusion holds only on Fashion (−0.59). The MNIST (and qd_a) pairs belong to ggbt's out-of-fold fit, which got stacker weight 0.
problems.correction: 'On Fashion-MNIST the most gain per drawn pair goes to contrasts of very different silhouettes (trouser–boot 5.8×, shirt–sneaker 4.9×), and similar classes get almost none (T-shirt–dress 0.01, sandal–boot 0.02, T-shirt–shirt 0.04). Elsewhere there is no such pattern: qd_dev's top class pair is grapes–soccer ball (5.3×), two round shapes and its third most confused pair. MNIST's pairs (1–2 4.0×, 0–1 3.5×) are from ggbt's out-of-fold fit, which has stacker weight 0.'

The stacker weights members, not individual characters. What is small is the total weight (median 0.35).

problems.correction: "On the 10 suites with network results (all but dlfamdev), v3's suite means against the per-suite best network range from -1.50 to -2.44, and a network is clearly better on one target only (h6_00, ...)." Delete the \todo.

problems.location: What is in-sample: "v3's code path there is v1's, frozen in Part 8 before HELDOUT2 was fixed."
problems.problem: The order is reversed. HELDOUT2 was fixed in commit 04a215b2 (26 Oct 06:05 UTC), "before any Part 8 design work" (study/hybrid/HYBRID.md l.65; data.py comment "fixed before any hybrid was designed"). v1 was designed and frozen after that, then run on HELDOUT2 once.
problems.correction: "...v3's code path there is v1's. HELDOUT2 was fixed before any Part 8 design work (commit 04a215b2), and v1 was frozen before it was run there, so HELDOUT2 is held out for that code."

problems.location: "On a fresh 12-target Boolean suite (d=30), drawn from a family written by an agent blind to the design, v3 needs clearly less data..." (also intro.tex 'Held-out toy suite' bullet: "12 targets drawn from the blind family of Part 9")
problems.problem: The family is blind to the Part 9 (v2) design only (FAMILY.md: "did not see the learner's design"). It is not blind to v3's toy component. The Part 10 toy builder developed on dlheld6 and dlfamdev, two other draws from this family (p10_sum/DESIGN.md l.17). v1.3's weighted class u = t + a*tau, with a in {±2,±3} and tau a literal, a parity of two inputs or an AND of two literals, is exactly the family's S4(a) stratum (FAMILY.md §3). In addition, v3 equals v2 on dlheld7: mean -0.004, 0 targets clearly changed. So the toy result does not test the Part 10 change.
problems.correction: Abstract: "...drawn from a family written in Part 9 by an agent blind to the Part 9 design (v3's toy component was developed on two other draws of the same family), v3 needs clearly less data ... and more on none; v2 does the same (v3/v2 mean -0.004)." Intro: add "The family was blind to Part 9's design, not to v3's: the Part 10 toy builder developed on dlheld6 and dlfamdev."

problems.location: "The mod-3 targets fail because they have no weight at those degrees, although their block would pass the test at 134–155 times the threshold."
problems.problem: Two problems. (1) It is factually wrong for fd_10. VERIFICATION.json (verify-reading:toy C6 and other_problems 7) found W1 = 4e-5 and single and pair coefficients of about 0.002 for fd_10; "zero in expectation" holds only for h6_00 and f7_05 (toy_timing.csv: fd_10 W2 = 0.0002). (2) "fail because" is a causal reading of a descriptive, seed-0 analysis with no ablation.
problems.correction: "On the three mod-3 targets the search never proposes the block, consistent with their near-zero weight at those degrees (W1+W2 <= 0.0002; zero for h6_00 and f7_05), although at n=16384 the true block would pass the test at 134–155 times the threshold."

problems.location: 'What DFG learns' bullet: "The three residue classes mod 3 have no weight there, and the search never proposes their block..."
problems.problem: Same factual error as in the abstract: fd_10 has W1 = 4e-5, W2 = 0.0002, and coefficients of about 0.002 (VERIFICATION.json verify-reading:toy C6 and other 7). The bullet also does not say that the analysis is seed 0.
problems.correction: "The three residue classes mod 3 have almost no weight there (W1+W2 <= 0.0002; exactly zero for h6_00 and f7_05), and the search never proposes their block...". Add "(seed 0)" to the bullet.

problems.location: 'Where neither has a foothold': "The residue classes mod 3 of 10–14-input counts have no Fourier weight at degrees 1 and 2."
problems.problem: Wrong for fd_10, whose single and pair coefficients are about 0.002, nonzero but undetectable before n of roughly 10^6 (VERIFICATION.json verify-reading:toy C6 and other 7). The verifier corrected this wording.
problems.correction: "...have almost no Fourier weight at degrees 1 and 2 (none for h6_00 and f7_05; coefficients of about 0.002 for fd_10, undetectable at the study's n)."

problems.location: "...and the data needed beyond that grows as the residual's degree-1 and degree-2 statistics point to the block more weakly."
problems.problem: The sentence states the measured quantity as a mechanism. What was measured is the Spearman correlation (-0.86 over the 25 pure targets, seed 0) between the delay and the target's share of variance at Fourier degrees 1–2, (W1+W2)/(1-W0) (toy_timing.csv low2; fig_interp.json). No residual statistic was measured.
problems.correction: "...and the data needed beyond that grows as the target's share of variance at Fourier degrees 1–2 shrinks (Spearman -0.86 over those 25)."

problems.location: "On tabular data v3 is a classical stack whose margin over MLPs is not significant."
problems.problem: Too broad. Against the baseline mlp the sign test is significant: 9 of 10 HELDOUT2 datasets (p=0.021) and 10 of 11 Part 7 datasets (p=0.012). On the Part 7 set it is also significant against mlp_strong (p=0.012) (LEARNER_RESULTS). The p=0.11 result is for mlp_best, mlp_reg and mlp_strong on HELDOUT2.
problems.correction: "On tabular data v3 is a classical stack whose margin over the hindsight-best MLP is not significant (lower mean error on 8 of 10 fresh datasets, sign test p=0.11)."

problems.location: "...can beat permutation-invariant MLP ensembles that spend 2–9 times its FLOP budget, and can tie the one whose time per fit matches its own."
problems.problem: The 9.2-budget ensemble is mlp_xl, the one v3 only ties. v3 beats mlp_strong (2.0 budgets) at 6 of 6 cells and mlp_wide (5.0 budgets) at 5 of 6 (a tie at qd_c 60000) (tab_images_compute, tab_images_summary). It also leaves out that ggbt's bank contains 300 prototype-pair projections, not only subset sums.
problems.correction: "...can beat MLP ensembles that spend 2.0 and 5.0 times its FLOP budget (mlp_strong at all six held-out cells, mlp_wide at five of six), and ties the 1024-wide ensemble, which spends 9.2 budgets and about as much time per fit."

problems.location: Images bullet 1: "v3 is clearly better than it at both (16.5% and 11.9% lower error), so v3's bars add something an MLP on v2's features does not have."
problems.problem: The inference goes further than the evidence. v3 against v2 is a tie at both cells (9.1% and 6.4% lower), so the step from v2-ties-mlp_pool to v3-beats-mlp_pool rests on differences inside the tie band. mlp_pool is seed 0 at both cells (mlp_pool__qd_c.json), compared there with v3's 3-seed mean at n=10^4. cgbt differs from ggbt in three ways (bars, no pairs, column fraction 0.05), so the gain cannot be attributed to the bars alone.
problems.correction: "v3 is clearly better than it at both (16.5% and 11.9% lower error; mlp_pool seed 0), while v3 and v2 tie there. This is consistent with cgbt's bank adding something an MLP on v2's features does not have, but it is not a test of the bars."

problems.location: Contribution 3: "a comparison of v3 with every reference on every toy suite and real dataset of the study"
problems.problem: Not true as stated. v3 has no MNIST run: no p10_codes-dev__mnist or hyb_portfolio3__mnist file, and compare_learner.py leaves MNIST out. dlfamdev has no network, lin or hgb runs. v1 has no toy run on dlfamdev or dlheld7. hgb has no run on designed or dlsymdev (LEARNER_RESULTS shows '–').
problems.correction: "a comparison of v3 with every reference that was run, on every toy suite and every real dataset of the study except MNIST (where v3 enters only the interpretability analysis), with the status of each set for v3 stated".

problems.location: Builders paragraph: "Development used validation rows of the development sets only, never a test set."
problems.problem: False for the toy builder. p10_sum/DESIGN.md §4 says its portfolio checks were scored "on the harness's points" and compared with "v2's stored fits". These are test errors of development suites, e.g. h6_10 n* 171 against 702, and sym7 at n=64 0.457 → 0.000. Only the two image builders used validation rows only.
problems.correction: "The image builders used validation rows of the development sets only. The toy builder scored its DFG-alone checks on fresh validation draws, and its portfolio checks on the toy harness's test points of the development suites (designed, dlsymdev, dlfamdev, dlheld6). No builder used a held-out set."

problems.location: Budget paragraph: "Every member's FLOPs are counted (library trees by an audited per-tree formula), and members whose projected cost would exceed 90% of the budget are skipped."
problems.problem: Only ggbt and cgbt use the audited lgb_tree_flops (learner.py l.365). Part 8's gbt member is still charged by its original formula (fit_gbt l.177: 10nd per tree plus 8·31·d·255). Part 9's audit found that formula too low by 1.14–1.46× at n=3000, and results_images.tex l.157 and discussion.tex say "v3 keeps that charge", so the two sections contradict each other. The guard is also cumulative: a member is skipped if spent + projected cost > 0.9 of the budget (0.95 for lin).
problems.correction: "Every member's FLOPs are counted: the image boosters by the compute audit's per-tree formula, and Part 8's gbt member by its original formula, which Part 9's audit found low by 1.14–1.46× at n=3000. A member is skipped when its projected cost would take the total above 90% of the budget (95% for logistic regression)."

problems.location: Sum-block variants: "split blocks rewrite a mixed-sign block as |t_A−t_B|"
problems.problem: The code works differently (dfg13.py l.767–778). The split move builds a block on the positive-sign inputs (t_A, folded if the candidate was) and searches a second block over the joint cells with it, initialised with the negative-sign inputs. The result is a product block, a function of (t_A, t_B), not of |t_A−t_B|.
problems.correction: "split blocks replace a mixed-sign candidate by the product block of its positive-sign part and a block searched on its negative-sign part (the joint cells of t_A and t_B)".

problems.location: Block search: "Candidates come from four sources: ... greedy growth from the strongest pairs; at n≤128 (v1.3), a width-32 beam"
problems.problem: Incomplete. The code also grows greedily from the 2 strongest single inputs (sum_seeds=(2,3,2)). In the additive search it adds v1.3's weighted candidates: weighted eigenvector prefixes, tau-first on the strongest pair, and extensions of the 2 best refined candidates (l.231–285, 443–491). The beam runs only in the first additive search of a round.
problems.correction: "...greedy growth from the 3 strongest pairs and the 2 strongest single inputs; in the additive search, v1.3's weighted candidates (weighted eigenvector prefixes, an inner term on the strongest pair, extensions of the two best unweighted candidates); and at n≤128, in the first additive search of a round, a width-32 beam over (S,s)."

problems.location: Where it cannot work: "...is invisible to the seeds, however large n is."
problems.problem: Too strong. fd_10's single and pair coefficients are about 0.002, which would become detectable at n of roughly 10^6 (VERIFICATION.json verify-reading:toy C6). Only h6_00 and f7_05 have zero low-degree statistics in expectation.
problems.correction: "...is invisible to the seeds at every n of the study's grid (≤16384); for h6_00 and f7_05 the seeds' statistics are zero in expectation."

problems.location: "It is not free: at d=30 no 7-input block can pass below n≈75."
problems.problem: Computed from eq. (blocktest), with k=7 and no modulators: tau_7 = 27.6 nats, so the threshold is 66.8 at m=1, 72.1 at m=2 and 76.5 at m=3 (70.3–84.1 with four modulators). Since T ≤ n, the hard bound is n > 67. The figure ≈75 holds for three or more occupied groups (it comes from p9_sum/DESIGN.md §5b).
problems.correction: "...no 7-input block can pass below n≈67, and below n≈75 with three or more value groups."

problems.location: tab:members rows gbt/et ("on the raw columns ... always"), lin_C ("C∈{0.05,1}"), dfg_forced; and "Which members run is decided by the input type alone."
problems.problem: Several details do not match learner.py. ExtraTrees is fitted on the standard encoding Zs (z-scored, ±1, one-hot; fit_et(Zs,...)), not on the raw columns. gbt subsamples rows 0.5 and columns 0.25 per tree when nd>10^7. lin uses only C=1 for n>10^4 (lin_one_n). dfg_forced runs only at n≤512 (cv_n). Which members run also depends on n and on the budget guard.
problems.correction: Write "gbt: LightGBM on the raw columns (categoricals as categories; rows 0.5, columns 0.25 per tree when nd>10^7); et: ExtraTrees on the standardized encoding", "lin_C: C∈{0.05,1} (C=1 only for n>10^4)" and "dfg_forced: n≤512". Change the sentence to "Which members run is decided by the input type, n and the budget."

problems.location: DFG intro: "Training stops when a round admits nothing, when every training sign is right, or at 75% of the budget."
problems.problem: Incomplete. DFG also stops after 8 rounds (rounds=8) or when least squares has no room left (p ≤ n/2) (dfg13.py l.594–598, 823–825). The 75% cap applies to DFG's own budget share, not to the fit's budget.
problems.correction: "...when every training sign is right, after 8 rounds, when the feature count reaches n/2, or once 75% of DFG's budget share is spent."

problems.location: tab:discrete (and abstract: "No member fits a feature direction by gradient descent.")
problems.problem: The table leaves out the lin member. Its weights on the standardized inputs are a continuous linear direction, fitted by L-BFGS (a gradient-based quasi-Newton method) on convex log-loss. The prototype pairs are also two random training points of different classes, which the table does not say.
problems.correction: Add a row: "logistic regression lin: weights on standardized inputs | convex log-loss (L-BFGS) | yes (linear readout on the raw inputs)", and write "two random training points of different classes". Abstract: "No member learns features by gradient descent; the continuous fits are convex linear readouts (including a logistic regression on the inputs), tree leaf values and stacking weights."

problems.location: What is in-sample: "...and the image builders on qd_dev, qd_a and Fashion-MNIST."
problems.problem: Incomplete. Both image builders' DESIGN.md files list validation rows of qd_dev, qd_a, qd_b and Fashion-MNIST. p10_codes also used MNIST for topology diagnostics, and p10_hier used optdigits.
problems.correction: "...and the image builders on validation rows of qd_dev, qd_a, qd_b and Fashion-MNIST (and MNIST for topology diagnostics)."

problems.location: Earlier versions: "v1 (Part 8) and v2 (Part 9) are run as references wherever their predictions can differ from v3's."
problems.problem: v1 (hyb_portfolio-perm) has no toy run on dlfamdev or dlheld7, where its DFG v1.1 would differ from v3's (no toy__hyb_portfolio-perm__dlheld7.json; the v1 column is '–' in LEARNER_RESULTS).
problems.correction: "v2 is run on every toy suite and held-out image set, and v1 on every image set and on every toy suite except dlfamdev and dlheld7."

problems.location: Standard tasks: "There are 3 seeds, except on images at n≥30000, where every learner runs seed 0 only."
problems.problem: A caveat is missing. The control mlp_pool and the context cnn ran seed 0 only at every n (mlp_pool__qd_c.json; cnn__qd_c/qd_a.json, note "seed 0 only"), and mlp_xl ran only at 60000. At n=10^3 and 10^4 they are therefore compared with v3's 3-seed means.
problems.correction: Add: "The control mlp_pool and the context cnn ran seed 0 only at every n, and mlp_xl at n=60000 only."

problems.location: tab:status rows
problems.problem: Three rows are inaccurate. (1) random was a Part 6 development check (compare_learner.py role), not a set "held out for earlier versions". (2) For designed/dlsymdev/dlfamdev, "variants run there" hides that dlfamdev has no network runs. (3) In the tabular row, "where DFG runs" suggests v1 has no DFG there, but v1 runs DFG v1.1 on kr_vs_kp and mushroom. kr_vs_kp was also the toy builder's tabular development check.
problems.correction: (1) Split the row: "random: development check in Part 6; dlheld–dlheld5: held out for earlier versions". (2) Write "variants run there (none on dlfamdev)". (3) Write "...except on kr_vs_kp and mushroom, where DFG v1.3 replaces v1's DFG v1.1 (kr_vs_kp: the toy builder's development check)".

problems.location: Tasks, dlfamdev/dlheld7: "Each slot draws its accept set uniformly from five types, one of them a residue class mod 3 or 4."
problems.problem: Not true for every slot. In FAMILY.md §3, the S4(a) inner-term form uses only a threshold or a centred band. The five-type ACCEPT draw applies to the S1–S3 and S4(b) blocks.
problems.correction: "Each block's accept set is drawn uniformly from five types, one of them a residue class mod 3 or 4, except in the inner-term form u = s + a·tau, which uses a threshold or a band."

problems.location: 'Images: locality recovered from data': "A 2-D embedding of the pooling-set graph matches the grid with R^2 0.97–0.99" and "the bars are short, nearly straight runs along it"
problems.problem: (1) The R² range is true only at n≥3000. tab_interp_img_geom gives k=4 union R² 0.84 at qd_dev n=1000, 0.97/0.97 at 3000/10000 and 0.99 on qd_a (MNIST 0.92). (2) On QuickDraw the bars are exact lattice lines in only 33–42% of cases (L=2) and 16–25% (L=4); 96% (L=2) but 63% (L=4) lie within 1 px of a line. The verifier noted that straightness comes from the construction and the data (verify-reading:image C3).
problems.correction: "...matches the grid with R² 0.97–0.99 at n≥3000 (0.84 at n=1000; seed 0)". Write "...and the 5-pixel bars lie within a pixel of a straight run in about 96% of cases (the 9-pixel bars in 63%)".

problems.location: 'Why it works', second paragraph: "the seed-0 10% error point falls in the doubling just below the first grid size at which the model holds the exact block. What sets the data cost is when the search first proposes the block."
problems.problem: The first statement holds for the 22 found pure targets; the 3 mod-3 targets are never found. Because n_struct is a grid value, it is mostly a matter of grid resolution (verify-reading:toy other 6). "What sets the data cost" is a causal reading with no ablation; the verifier asked for 'consistent with' (C7).
problems.correction: "...and on each of the 22 found targets the seed-0 10% error point lies within the doubling below the first grid size at which the model holds the exact block. This is consistent with the data cost being set by when the search first proposes the block [Heuristic]."

problems.location: Limits, 'Small held-out sets': "...and only 5 of its 10 wins need feature search."
problems.problem: "need feature search" is a reading. What was measured is that on 5 of the 10 wins default hgb or lin already beats nets_best clearly (f7_02, f7_04, f7_06, f7_10, f7_11).
problems.correction: "...and on 5 of its 10 wins default gradient boosting or logistic regression already beats the networks."

problems.location: Limits, first bullet: "h5s7 ... with 0.015 of its variance at degrees 1–2"; "h5s1 is learned by no learner"
problems.problem: (1) The share of variance is (W1+W2)/(1−W0) = 0.0166 (toy_timing.csv low2). W1+W2 = 0.0153 is the share of total Fourier weight. (2) v3's seed-0 run does reach 10% error on h5s1 (n*_0 ≈ 14263, n_struct 16384); only the 3-seed n* is 'never'.
problems.correction: "...with 0.017 of its variance at degrees 1–2..." and "h5s1 reaches 10% error in no learner's 3-seed mean (v3 seed 0 at n≈14000)..."

problems.location: 'Where neither has a foothold': "The networks mostly fail too: none learns f7_05, and only the most regularized variant learns h6_00"
problems.problem: A caveat is missing. The third mod-3 target, fd_10, is in dlfamdev, which has no network runs.
problems.correction: Add "(fd_10, in dlfamdev, has no network runs)".

problems.location: 'What kind of learner': "Pixels, sums over blobs of 4, 9 and 16 mutually correlated pixels, and sums over 5- and 9-pixel bars ... Trees split on them"
problems.problem: S_i(k) is the set of the k pixels most correlated with pixel i, not a set of mutually correlated pixels (pool_sets). Bars have up to 5 or 9 pixels, because they stop early. ggbt's bank also has 300 prototype-pair projections (x_a−x_b)·x, which are not subset sums.
problems.correction: "Pixels, sums over the 4, 9 and 16 pixels most correlated with each pixel, sums over bars of up to 5 and 9 pixels along lines recovered from the correlations, and (in ggbt) 300 differences of two training images..."

problems.location: "On images the main members are gradient-boosted trees..."; "On images the pooling sets are local neighbourhoods of the true pixel grid"
problems.problem: (1) At n=1000 the pooled k-NN votes carry more stacking weight than the boosters (qd_c gknn 0.38 against cgbt 0.27; qd_d 0.30 against 0.23; qd_dev 0.44 against 0.32; tab_images_stack, tab_interp_img_stack), and stacking weights are not influence. (2) The locality finding holds on QuickDraw and MNIST. On Fashion-MNIST 7% of the 4-pixel sets include a mirror-image pixel, and the Isomap R² is 0.13.
problems.correction: "On images the members that carry most stacking weight at n≥10^4 are gradient-boosted trees..." and "On QuickDraw and MNIST the pooling sets are local neighbourhoods of the true pixel grid..."

problems.location: 'What the image members encode': "...and on QuickDraw and MNIST it takes over the old booster's stacking weight."
problems.problem: In the analysis this is compared with v2 only at qd_dev n=10000; there is no v2 analysis on MNIST. The stacker splits weight between two nearly collinear boosters on one holdout, and weights on log-probabilities are not contributions (verify-reading:image C4).
problems.correction: "...and in the analysed QuickDraw and MNIST fits it holds most of the boosters' stacking weight (0.32–0.56 against ggbt's 0–0.09; v2's ggbt had 0.41 at qd_dev n=10^4)."

problems.location: Parts 1–5 bullet: "d^{1.0}, d^{1.9} and d^{2.4} for k=2,3,4. That is close to the leap and correlational-SQ rate d^{k-1}"; opening: "a study that has asked this question in ten parts"
problems.problem: (1) The README §3.1 says this is close to d^{k-1} for k≤3 and somewhat below it for k=4 (2.40 against 3). learner.tex repeats "about d^{k-1} samples". (2) Parts 1–5 asked what gradient descent does on Boolean targets. The question whether a discrete learner can match it begins in Part 6.
problems.correction: (1) "...close to the leap and correlational-SQ rate d^{k-1} for k≤3, and somewhat below it for k=4". (2) "...the latest learner of a ten-part study, whose Parts 6–10 have asked this question."
